newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BETIS CAN HALT RUNAWAY REAL MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BETIS CAN HALT RUNAWAY REAL MADRID.

text.p: The teams with the best home and away records in Spain meet head on this weekend as leaders Real Madrid take on third-placed surprise side Real Betis.
Although the season is only just past halfway, Saturday's game in the capital is seen by many as the last chance for Real Madrid to be caught. They boast an eight-point advantage over Barcelona.
Barcelona's challenge has evaporated in the past few games and on current form they seem unlikely to recover in time.
But another two points back with a game in hand are a Betis side who have gone from strength to strength. Like Real Madrid they are unbeaten away and are the only team to have scored in every game.
"If we win in Madrid then we'd make the championship a lot more tightly-run," said Betis manager Lorenzo Serra Ferrer.
Serra Ferrer's players have won five consecutive games, all by at least two goals, since squandering a 2-0 lead to go down 4-2 to Barcelona.
Betis have become experts in turning around away games, in many cases after being awarded a penalty, or having an opponent sent off.

In many cases the crucial foul has been made upon former Real Madrid man Alfonso Perez. Alfonso -- who scored twice in Spain's 4-0 win over Malta on Wednesday -- is expected to miss the game after collecting his fifth booking of the season last weekend.
Betis have appealed against the suspension, which Serra Ferrer called "a little bit exaggerated".
Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello has said that he misses Alfonso, who moved to Betis on loan last season, returned to Madrid and was eventually bought back over the summer.
But it is arguable whether there would be room in the Real Madrid line-up, even for Spain's leading forward.
Capello has relied on the goals of Predrag Mijatovic and Davor Suker to paper over his tactical problems, while teenage support player Raul Gonzalez continues to dazzle.
Raul put in an extraordinary performance as he led his side from 1-0 down to a 4-1 victory over champions Atletico last month.
Since then Real have piled on the pressure, and despite falling in the cup to Barcelona, they seem to have Bobby Robson's side against the ropes.
A Real Madrid victory would cast Barcelona 11 points adrift, and increase even further the pressure on the beleaguered former England coach ahead of Sunday's game against Racing Santander.
A Betis win would leave them as favourites for one of the two European Cup berths -- a fine effort for a team who only returned to the first division in 1994.
"We've got a lot to win, and not much to lose," said Betis defender Tomas Olias, scorer of four vital away goals this season.
